newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas says profit under pressure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas says profit under pressure.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Wednesday that an increase in 1996/97 earnings would depend on a higher second half result.
The national airline also said its current year profit would be affected by the stronger Australian dollar and the recent hike in fuel prices.
Qantas chairman Gary Pemberton told shareholders at the annual meeting that the market had softened against expectations in early 1996/97 trading, with weakness in yields and loads.

"In addition, the high fuel costs and the high Australian dollar will have a negative impact on our profitability," Pemberton said, adding that Qantas was looking to increase cost savings beyond the A$330 million target already announced.
"With all the usual cautions and qualifications, we are still looking to improve on last year's profit," he said.
"This prediction is not without downside risk and the extent of any improvement will be largely determined by market conditions in the second half of the year," Pemberton said.

He said that Qantas, which was now in its second financial year as a public company after being sold by the Australian government, would focus on better use of assets, lower costs and capital expenditure, and lower gearing to manage operations in the current year.
Qantas achieved a 37 percent rise in 1995/96 (July-June) net profit to A$246.2 million. It is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
